title: Docxodus workflow evaluation scenario v1
description: One deterministic document-workflow task: a fixture, a machine-readable instruction expressed as agent-surface tool calls, and the invariants that decide whether the run passed. Adding a scenario means writing invariants — a scenario with no invariant assertions is rejected by the runner rather than silently passing.

id.description: Stable identifier. Also the artifact directory name on failure.

intent.description: What a human asked for, in one sentence. This is the prompt an agent run would be given; the scripted caller ignores it and executes steps directly, which is what separates engine correctness from model planning quality.

fixture.description: Name of a build script under eval/fixtures. Fixtures are constructed programmatically through the same step format, so the corpus carries no third-party document bytes.

trackedChanges.description: How the session records the scripted caller's own edits — docxodus_open's trackedChanges.

tool.description: An MCP tool name. The scripted caller drives the agent surface, not the .NET API, so the engine baseline is measured where an agent would meet it.

target.description: Resolved to an anchor id by docxodus_search before the call, then injected into args. Targeting by content rather than by a chained response keeps a step independent of the previous step's result shape.

targets.description: For tools taking several anchors (ranges, moves, bookmarks): each key names the argument that receives its resolved anchor id, each value is a target resolved exactly like `target`. The key already names the argument, so `as` is rejected inside these targets. May be combined with `target` when the argument names do not collide.

args.description: The tool's own arguments, minus sessionId (supplied by the runner) and minus the argument(s) that `target`/`targets` fill in.

index.description: Which match to use, in document order. The runner fails the scenario when the match count is smaller than index+1, so a fixture drift surfaces as a scenario error rather than as a silently different target.

as.description: Which argument receives the resolved anchor, e.g. cellAnchorId for table tools.

taskCompletion.description: Did the intended change land? Asserted over the saved deliverable, not over tool return values.

targetPrecision.description: Did it change only what it was asked to? Counted as distinct anchors in the #457 semantic change set from the opening package to the saved state. Must declare at least one bound: an empty targetPrecision bounds nothing.

collateral.description: Was unrelated package state preserved? Counted from #456 package manifests of the opening and saved packages.

textPreserved.description: Content that must survive untouched — the near-miss occurrences a careless edit would also catch.

changedPartsMustBeWithin.description: Part URIs the #457 change set may touch, exactly as the change set reports them (leading slash: "/word/document.xml"). Any changed part outside this allowlist fails the scenario — the identity assertion that turns 'how many parts changed' into 'the right parts changed'. A misspelled entry fails loudly rather than passing, because the real changed part is then outside the list.

trackedRevisions.description: Live tracked-change markup in the delivered session, read through docxodus_track_changes list. This is how a scenario asserts a pre-existing reviewer's revision is still live outside the reversibility path.

comments.description: Comments in the delivered session, read through docxodus_comment list. Replies are entries carrying parentAnchorId; resolved state is the tool's own resolved flag — only what the tool reports is assertable.

redline.description: Assertions over a redline document a docxodus_compare step wrote. The runner opens fromPath in a fresh session and reads docxodus_track_changes list — the same agent-surface view trackedRevisions uses for the delivered session — so the bounds describe the produced file itself, not the compare tool's own summary.

fromPath.description: The workspace path a step wrote the redline to — the same path vocabulary steps use for docxodus_save and docxodus_compare.

validity.description: Is the deliverable structurally valid? The #463 deliverable gate, run with the opening bytes as baseline.

reversibility.description: For tracked-change scenarios: does the redline accept to the intended final and reject to the baseline? The #464 proof, with the intended final derived by accepting every revision.

mode.description: acceptAll derives the intended final by accepting every revision in the deliverable, then proves the deliverable against it and the opening package.

mustSucceed.description: Require full package equivalence on both paths. Opt-in: a session-authored redline is not yet expected to reach it, because the intended final has to be derived and the proof would then be scoring that derivation. See eval/README.md.

pathsMustComplete.description: Both proof paths must run to completion. Defaults on.

preExistingMustBePreserved.description: Resolving only the generated revisions must leave pre-existing review state intact on both paths. Defaults on.

rejectMustRestoreBaseline.description: Rejecting only the generated revisions must be semantically equivalent to the opening package. Unlike the accept path, the baseline is stated up front rather than derived, so this asserts restoration itself. Defaults on.

rendering.description: Rendering regression, HTML-only in this scaffold. Generated-PDF fidelity is #443's ratchet and is deliberately not a dependency here.
